info.title: Tessera API
info.description: Anonymous file courier. Upload a file or a note, hand out a retrieval code, and the payload destroys itself once it expires or runs out of retrievals.

get.summary: Reports which optional parts of the service this instance exposes.
get.description:
# Errors

Infallible in practice; the signature matches the rest of the API so that a
future version can start failing without changing every caller.

get.summary: Reports whether the service is ready to take traffic.
get.description:
Deliberately both a liveness and a readiness probe: the process only reaches
[`ServiceStatus::Ready`] once migrations have run, and it flips to
[`ServiceStatus::Draining`] the moment a shutdown signal arrives, so an
orchestrator can stop routing before the listener actually closes.

# Errors

Returns [`Error::Unavailable`] (503) while starting up or draining, and when
the database round-trip fails.

503.description: Starting up, draining, or a dependency is unreachable

Capabilities.description:
Body of `GET /api/v1/capabilities`.

# Why this endpoint exists

`openapi.json` is a build artefact: it describes every endpoint the software
has. Which of them an *instance* exposes is a runtime decision its operator
made. A single-page app generated from the contract therefore cannot know
whether to render a login button — the contract says login exists, and on
this deployment it may not.

So the contract describes the whole surface and this reports the subset in
force. It is deliberately unauthenticated: a client needs the answer before
it can know whether logging in is even possible.

accounts.description:
Whether accounts exist at all on this instance.

`false` means there is no registration, no login and no session — the
shape for a personal instance behind a VPN.

admin.description:
Whether the administrative endpoints are mounted.

The administration front-end is a separate deployment, so this says only
that the API half is present.

anonymous_upload.description:
Whether a caller without a session may upload.

Independent of [`accounts`](Self::accounts): an instance can have
accounts *and* accept anonymous uploads, which is the default.

max_upload_bytes.description: Longest accepted request body, in bytes.

password_min_length.description:
Shortest password this instance accepts, so a client can say so before
the round trip rather than after it.

registration.description:
Who may create an account. Meaningless when
[`accounts`](Self::accounts) is `false`.

version.description:
Version of the running server, for a client that wants to warn about a
mismatch with the contract it was generated from.

ErrorBody.description: The JSON body returned for every non-2xx response.

code.description: Stable identifier the client can branch on.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Never contains internal details.

ErrorCode.description:
Stable, machine-readable identifier for an [`Error`].

Clients branch on this; the human-readable `message` is free to change.

build_rev.description:
Commit the running binary was built from, or `unknown` outside a git
checkout. Between releases this is what identifies a build.

status.description: Where the process is in its lifecycle.

uptime_seconds.description: Whole seconds since the process started.

ServiceStatus.description:
Where the process is in its lifecycle.

Load balancers and `docker healthcheck` need to distinguish "still migrating"
from "draining" from "healthy"; a bare 200/500 cannot express that.
